newsitem.title: CANADA: Saskatchewan Wheat Pool increases oat mill stake.
newsitem.headline: Saskatchewan Wheat Pool increases oat mill stake.

text.p: Canada's largest grain handler said on Monday it paid C$14 million to raise its ownership stake in Canada's largest oat processor and exporter, a Saskatchewan Wheat Pool statement said.
As a result of the increased SWP ownership, Can-Oat Milling will build a new groating mill near Saskatoon, Sask., which will produce 72,000 tonnes of milled oats a year.
The additional equity was purchased through a combination of cash and the transfer of SWP's Saskatoon North elevator to Can-Oat, the statement said.
Construction of the mill was forecast at C$17.2 million.
"The potential exists to use the existing cleaning capabilities at Saskatoon to develop new markets for double re-clean oats and selected quality oats," the statment said.
Can-Oat's existing mill in Portage-la-Prairie, Man., has an annual capacity of 125,000 tonnes and produces 75,000 tonnes.
Can-Oat is jointly owned by SWP, Manitoba Pool Elevators, Can-Oat Holdings B.C. Ltd. and A.R. Holdings.
